name: Home and remote work
purpose: hybrid and remote work, wellbeing and switching off, security and scams at home, ergonomics at home, family life

identity.place: A 1930s semi-detached house on a quiet, tree-lined suburban road at the edge of a temperate city, bought and slowly modernised by the household that lives in it now (two working adults, a child of about eight, a dog). Two storeys under a hipped tiled roof, a two-storey canted bay at the front, a round-arched open porch, the old back dining room knocked through to the kitchen to make one long kitchen-diner facing the garden, and the small third bedroom over the front door turned into a study. The front of the house faces east-north-east, the garden west-south-west. About 2.6 m from floor to ceiling downstairs and 2.45 m upstairs.
architecture: outside: red-brown brick on the ground floor in stretcher bond, cream pebbledash render on the first floor, a hipped roof of red-brown clay plain tiles, a brick chimney stack on the party wall shared with the other half of the pair
a two-storey canted bay at the front of the living room and the main bedroom; beside it a round-arched open porch with a red quarry-tiled floor and one tiled step, sheltering the front door

windows are timber casements kept and repaired from the 1930s: cream-painted opening lights in dark green-painted frames, side-hung lower lights with a row of small top-hung upper lights above a transom at about 1.7 m; the upper lights carry clear leaded glass in a simple square and diamond pattern, the rest is plain glass

the front door is the original: a timber door painted deep sage green with a small horizontal oval window of rippled glass high up, two long panels below it, a brass letter plate and knob; long narrow side panels of rippled glass on both sides of it

inside: smooth plastered walls in warm off-white, with one wall in each room painted soft sage green or a muted colour; a plain picture rail downstairs at about 2.1 m, level with the top of the door architraves; plain moulded skirting boards; internal doors of the period, painted off-white, with one squarish panel at the top over three tall narrow vertical panels, and round brass knobs
floors: the hall keeps its oak woodblock in a herringbone; the living room and the upstairs rooms have sanded pine floorboards with rugs; the kitchen-diner has large pale grey stone-look tiles

fireplaces of the period stay as features: a tiled 1930s surround in the living room, and a plastered chimney breast with alcoves either side in the kitchen-diner, its old fireplace blocked and painted over
identity.materials: warm off-white and soft sage green painted plaster, sanded pine boards and oak woodblock, red-brown brick and cream pebbledash outside, oak and oak-veneer furniture of mixed ages, wool and cotton textiles in slate blue, oat and one mustard yellow, glazed tiles in the fireplace, brushed steel in the kitchen; deep sage green is the house's colour (the front door, the kitchen cabinet fronts, one wall per room), with signal red only on the few things that are red in life (a fire blanket's pull tabs in the kitchen)
inhabited: a family lives here: a child's drawings stuck to the fridge and a wall (shapes and colours only, no letters), a school bag on a chair, shoes by the door, a dog's bed and a chewed toy
work has moved in: a laptop and its charger cable, headphones, a work ID badge on a lanyard hung over a lamp or a chair, a notebook, a second mug gone cold

the ordinary infrastructure of a house: a white panel radiator under each window, light switches and plain socket plates (no pin shapes that pin a country), a ceiling smoke alarm in the hall and landing, a broadband router on a shelf with a few status lights
slight wear: a scuff along the skirting where the hoover hits, a rug corner turned up, a door that does not quite close, a faded patch on the sill where the sun falls
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; the ceilings are 2.6 m downstairs (1.5 times a person) and 2.45 m upstairs
internal doors are about 1.98 m by 0.76 m; the front door is about 1.98 m by 0.84 m; window sills are at about 0.85 to 0.9 m and window heads at about 2.1 m
a kitchen worktop is at 0.9 m (a 150 mm plinth, cabinets about 720 mm, the worktop about 30 mm) and 0.6 m deep; the tiled splashback runs about 0.45 m above it
a dining table and a desk top are at about 0.73 to 0.75 m, a dining chair seat at about 0.46 m, a sofa seat at about 0.43 m, a coffee table at about 0.42 m

a laptop on a stand lifts the top of its screen to about the sitter's eye height (about 1.15 to 1.2 m) with a separate keyboard and mouse on the desk; a video doorbell is mounted about 1.2 m above the step on the lock side of the front door
identity.default_light: A bright, overcast late morning in mid-autumn: soft daylight from the windows, a little warmer where it falls on the pine and the oak, slightly cool and blue in the corners away from the glass; when the cloud breaks, low sun reaches the front rooms in the morning and the kitchen-diner in the afternoon. Ceiling lights are off by day; a lamp is on only where the scene says so.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one house (each scene names the ones its camera can see): the cream timber casement with its small leaded upper lights, a deep or soft sage-green element, sanded pine or oak woodblock, a 1930s detail (the picture rail, the tiled fireplace, the round-arched porch, the panelled door), a slate-blue or mustard textile, a living houseplant.
avoid: a new-build box or a showroom home: no catalogue styling, nothing staged for a photograph
a mansion, a loft apartment or an American-style detached house with siding: this is a modest 1930s semi
real brands, logos, readable words or numbers (no house number on the door), flags, or plugs and sockets with pin shapes that pin a country
people in the sets (the cast is separate), and framed family photographs with faces (frames show an empty slot or a plain landscape)
mess that reads as neglect: the house is lived in and cared for
a laptop or screen facing a window or sitting with a window right behind it (glare): screens sit at about 90 degrees to the windows
modern uPVC windows or large single panes: the casements are the 1930s timber ones
identity.outside: Through the front windows: the quiet road, a grass verge with a young street tree, a low brick front wall, and the semis opposite (the same bays, porches and hipped roofs) under a pale sky. Through the back: a lawn, a timber fence, a small shed, an apple tree and the backs of the next road's houses. No landmarks, no signs.

The framed print hangs above the sofa between the two seats (x 383 to 652, y 207 to 378). The floor lamp stands at the sofa's right end (base x 1061, y 1006; shade about x 1061, y 418). Right of the corner, the party wall comes toward the camera: the far alcove's shelves with the books and the router (router about x 1402, y 598; the shelves' front edges from about x 1254 to 1512), then the chimney breast from x 1519 to beyond the right edge, with the tiled fireplace as the focal shape (the surround's far top corner at x 1534, y 594, the mantel at about y 545, the opening's far side at x 1646, y 869, running to x 1851, y 928 at its near side). The coffee table is cropped by the bottom edge at the lower middle (its far right corner about x 898, y 970). Free zones for the cast, nothing in front of head or chest: two people seated on the sofa, seen from the knees up, the left one (head top x 337, y 506; seat x 336, y 910) and the right one (head top x 744, y 505; seat x 757, y 882); both heads are seen against the plain sage back wall (behind points x 1.2 and 2.18 on the wall, 1.15 to 1.28 m high), about 130 px below the print and the right head about 317 px left of the lamp shade. What shows the room's height: the ceiling line crosses the top of the frame at the back corner and the picture rail runs along the back wall above the print.
scenes.light: Main set: mid-morning in mid-autumn, bright overcast. Daylight comes from the bay window behind the camera, so the room is lit from the front: the sofa, the sitters' faces and the fireplace tiles are evenly and softly lit, the glazed tiles catching a soft sheen. Soft shadows fall away from the camera onto the floor behind the coffee table and onto the back wall just behind the sofa and the lamp. The far alcove is a step darker. The floor lamp is off; the router shows two or three small green status lights. The room is about 4.7 m deep: no haze.
scenes.far: The shell: the back wall with the picture rail and the print; the party wall with the far alcove's shelves, books, plant and router, the chimney breast and the fireplace; the ceiling line; the floorboards; the sofa with its cushions (the sitters sit in it, in front of the far layer); the floor lamp beside it.
scenes.mid: The coffee table and what is on it, and the rug under it.
scenes.near: Nothing: the camera stands in the bay; the coffee table (mid) is the nearest thing, cropped by the bottom edge and continuing into the overscan.
details: a mustard cushion and a slate-blue one on the sofa, one squashed into the corner
a folded knitted throw over the sofa's left arm
on the coffee table: a phone face down, two mugs, a television remote and a small stack of post
the broadband router on the alcove shelf with two or three green status lights
a peace lily on the alcove shelf and a pair of reading glasses on the mantel
a child's toy car under the coffee table
scenes.keep_first: If space is short, keep the cushions, the throw, the phone and mugs on the coffee table and the router; drop the rest of the small things before adding anything else.
scenes.motifs_here: the tiled 1930s fireplace, the picture rail, the soft sage-green wall, the slate-blue sofa and the mustard cushion, sanded pine boards, the peace lily
slots: slot_print (the print's picture, frame about x 383 to 652, y 207 to 378)

anchor_seat_right (the sofa's right seat, about x 757, y 882)

variants: evening: night, the floor lamp on (a warm pool on the sofa's right end and the wall), the television's cool flicker from the right on the sofa and the sitters' faces, the bay's curtains drawn behind the camera so no window light
weekend: sun from the bay throws the shapes of its casements across the floor and the coffee table, newspapers and a cafetiere on the table
avoid: the print, the lamp, the room's corner or the shelves behind either head
a huge television on the back wall or a cinema room
a showroom sofa with perfectly plumped cushions
anything that makes the fireplace look Victorian (no cast-iron insert with a hood, no marble)
uses: checking work messages on the sofa late in the evening (switching off)
a call from someone claiming to be the bank asks for a code (a scam call at home)
a text about a missed delivery arrives with a link
securing the home router and the devices on the home network
a partner notices the signs of stress at the end of the day

scenes.what: the front of the house seen from its small front garden: the round-arched open porch with the sage-green front door standing open, the red quarry-tiled step, a video doorbell beside the door, the canted bay window to the right and the brick front wall to the left
scenes.for: the doorstep at home: deliveries and delivery scams, cold callers and doorstep fraud, checking who is there before opening, neighbours
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs along the front of the house from left to right as seen from the garden; y runs from the garden toward the house (the house front is at y 6.0); z up from the garden path. The low brick front wall and the gate to the pavement are behind the camera, at y 0.

House front (y 6.0): red-brown brick in stretcher bond up to a band at 2.9 m (the first floor), cream pebbledash above it (mostly above the frame). The house's left corner is at x -2.0, with a black downpipe at x -1.9; plain brick from there to the porch. A wheelie bin stands against the wall at x -1.4, y 5.3 (lid 1.07 m).

Porch: a round-arched opening in the house front from x 0 to 1.6, the arch springing at 1.95 m and its crown at 2.75 m, with a brick arch of headers; the porch is recessed 1.0 m (back wall at y 7.0), floored in red quarry tiles 0.15 m above the path, with the tiled edge of the step along the arch (y 5.75 to 6.0). A small lantern hangs from the porch ceiling (at x 0.8, y 6.5, 2.45 m). In the porch's back wall: the front door (x 0.38 to 1.22, 1.98 m high above the step) between two narrow side panels of rippled glass (x 0.08 to 0.36 and 1.24 to 1.52). The door is painted deep sage green with a small horizontal oval window of rippled glass high up and two long panels below, hinged on the right and standing open into the hall. The video doorbell is on the frame at the lock side, left of the door (x 0.25, 1.35 m above the path, 1.2 m above the step). A parcel lies on the porch tiles at x 1.25, y 6.3.

Inside the open door: the hall, 1.9 m wide (x -0.4 to 1.5) and 4.5 m long to its far end (y 11.5), its oak woodblock floor and the plain off-white left wall in deep shade; the stairs rise along the right wall, hidden by the right jamb.

The bay: the living room's canted bay projects 0.75 m from the front wall (front face at y 5.25) from x 1.95 to 4.4, with its casements from a sill at 0.85 m to a head at 2.1 m, cream-painted in dark green frames with leaded upper lights; a strip of lawn in front of it and a hydrangea in a bed at x 3.0, y 3.4 (about 1.0 m high).
The path: red and buff quarry tiles in a chequer, x -0.2 to 1.0, from the gate (behind the camera) to the step; a lawn either side.

Cast spots: the resident standing on the threshold in the open doorway (feet x 0.8, y 7.05, on the step level 0.15 m; head top 1.9 m above the path); a caller standing on the path's left edge 1 m in front of the step, facing the door in three-quarter (feet x -0.1, y 5.0; head top 1.75 m).

Camera: x 3.4, y 0.6 (standing on the lawn inside the front wall, to the right of the path), standing eye height 1.6 m, turned 24 degrees left of the y axis (toward the porch); lens like 35 mm (55 degrees across); no tilt; the horizon at 46 percent of the frame height.
scenes.camera: Standing eye height 1.6 m on the front lawn, to the right of the path, turned 24 degrees left toward the porch; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt, verticals stay vertical. Two-point perspective: horizon at y 497 (46 percent); lines running toward the house (the path's edges, the porch's side walls, the bay's sides) meet at x about 1781 on the horizon; lines along the house front (the brick courses, the render band, the step's edge, the bay's sill) run down gently to the left toward a vanishing point far off the left edge (x about -3182).
scenes.composition: The house front runs across the frame. Left: the plain brick front from the house's corner (a vertical at x 252, from the ground at y 911 up to the render band at y 161) with the downpipe beside it (x 272) and the wheelie bin standing in front of the wall near the corner (x 230, lid y 653, base y 969). The porch arch is the focal shape, left of centre: its left side at x 694 (ground y 964), its right side at x 1140 (ground y 1018), springing at about y 390 and its crown at x 905, y 143. Inside it, in shade, the porch's back wall with the open doorway (left jamb x 919, right jamb x 1128, head at about y 355, threshold at about y 880), the side panels of rippled glass either side, the video doorbell on the left of the door (x 889, y 561), the lantern hanging in the arch (x 967, y 254), and the parcel on the tiles (x 1067, y 891). The tiled step runs along the foot of the arch (from x 706, y 942 to x 1049, y 981); the chequered path comes toward the camera from it (from x 603 to 928 at the step), widening out of the bottom of the frame at the lower left. Right: the bay window, its left side at x 1176 (sill y 783, the bay running up out of the top past the render band) and its front face from x 1367 to beyond the right edge, glazing over a lawn strip; the render band crosses the top from x 252, y 161 to x 1251, y 63. The hydrangea stands at the lower right (top about x 1484, y 904), cropped by the bottom edge. Free zones for the cast, nothing in front of head or chest: (1) the resident in the open doorway, seen full length on the threshold (head top x 1026, y 417; feet x 1026, y 882), the head inside the door opening about 100 px from each jamb, seen against the dim, plain hall wall about 3 m inside (behind point on the hall's left wall at y 10.0, 1.85 to 2.04 m); (2) the caller on the path, seen full length from behind in three-quarter, facing the door (head top x 483, y 446; feet x 483, y 1039), the head against plain brick (behind point x -0.9 on the house front, 1.62 to 1.78 m high), 231 px right of the house corner and 211 px left of the arch. What shows the height: the arch and the bay rise past the render band, and the band and the pebbledash above it run out of the top of the frame; the first-floor windows are above the frame and are not drawn.
scenes.light: Main set: a bright late morning in mid-autumn with thin cloud. Soft sun from behind the camera's left (low, from the east-south-east) lights the brick front, the bay and the arch's right-hand reveal; shadows fall to the right and away from the camera: the wheelie bin's shadow onto the wall to its right, and the hydrangea's onto the lawn toward the right. The porch is in shade inside its arch, darker toward the back wall; the hall beyond the open door is in deep, even shade, its wall and its far end two close dark values with no detail. The lantern is off. The doorbell shows a small pale ring of light. The bay's glass shows a soft reflection of the sky and the street tree, not the room. No haze.
scenes.far: The house: the brick front with the downpipe, the render band and pebbledash, the porch with its arch, tiles, back wall, side panels, open door, doorbell, lantern and the parcel, the dim hall inside, the bay with its glazing, the wheelie bin, the lawn and the chequered path.
scenes.mid: Nothing between the camera and the cast except the ground: the path and the lawn are far.
scenes.near: Only the hydrangea in its bed at the lower right, cropped by the bottom edge (top about x 1484, y 904), in front of the bay's corner; it hides no cast zone.
details: a parcel on the porch tiles with a plain paper label (a slot, no writing)
a doormat inside the threshold and a pair of boots beside it on the hall floor
the video doorbell's small ring of light beside the door
a wheelie bin by the wall with its lid not quite closed
a potted bay tree in a terracotta pot on the porch tiles, left of the door
a few fallen leaves on the path and the step
scenes.keep_first: If space is short, keep the parcel, the doorbell, the bay tree in its pot and the wheelie bin; drop the rest of the small things before adding anything else.
scenes.motifs_here: the round-arched porch with its red quarry tiles, the sage-green front door (open into the hall, glimpsed through the rippled glass of the right side panel), the cream casements with leaded upper lights in the bay, the cream pebbledash above the brick, the potted bay tree
slots: slot_parcel_label (the parcel's label, on the parcel's top face, frame about x 1036 to 1096, y 870 to 883)
anchors: anchor_floor_y (the path at the caller's feet, about y 1039)
variants: door_closed: the front door shut (its oval window and two long panels, brass knob and letter plate), the parcel on the step, nobody home
evening: dusk, the porch lantern on (a warm pool on the tiles and the door), the bay window lit warm from inside, the sky deep blue, the doorbell's ring bright
rain: wet path and tiles with soft reflections, the parcel under the porch, an umbrella stand by the door
avoid: a house number, a name plate, a sign or any readable label
the arch's edge, the house corner or the downpipe behind the caller's head
bright light or any detail in the hall behind the resident's head
an American-style house with siding, a porch deck or a mailbox on a post
a courier's van or a branded parcel
uses: a courier asks for a signature and the resident checks the parcel before taking it
a caller claims to be from the water company and asks to come in (doorstep fraud)
checking the video doorbell before opening the door to a stranger
a text says a delivery was missed, but the parcel is already on the step
a neighbour drops by to talk about a worry

cast.role: remote and hybrid workers (varied ages and backgrounds), at home in everyday clothes
a partner, a child of about eight (C7 brief, age-accurate), an older parent visiting
a courier with a parcel and a handheld scanner, a cold caller with a lanyard and clipboard, a neighbour

objects.desk: a plain oak-veneer desk 1.2 by 0.6 m, its top 0.73 m high and about 25 mm thick, on four square legs joined by a shallow apron, with one slim drawer under the front edge; the laptop's charging cable runs to the desk's end and down to a plain socket plate low on the nearest wall
objects.desk chair: a plain home task chair: a five-spoke base on five castors, a gas-lift column, an upholstered seat about 0.47 m high with a rounded front edge, a fabric-covered back on a curved frame, two armrests on posts; smaller and plainer than an office chair
objects.laptop on a stand: a laptop about 0.32 by 0.22 m, open on a slim aluminium folding stand (two angled plates on a hinge) that lifts the top of its screen to about the sitter's eye height (1.15 to 1.2 m), its own keyboard tilted up and unused; the back of the lid is plain, no logo; a charging cable runs from its side
objects.keyboard and mouse: a separate flat keyboard about 0.43 by 0.13 m and a mouse about 0.11 m long, set in front of the laptop stand near the desk's front edge
objects.desk lamp: a spring-balanced desk lamp: a round weighted base, two jointed arms with exposed springs, a small conical metal shade with the bulb inside; about 0.45 m tall as set
objects.mug: a ceramic mug about 95 mm tall and 80 mm across with a loop handle; mugs in the house do not match
objects.phone: a plain smartphone about 150 by 72 mm in a dark case, lying face down unless a scene says otherwise; a screen facing up is a slot
objects.headphones: over-ear headphones: a padded headband and two oval ear cups on swivel yokes, about 0.18 m across
objects.notebook and pen: an A5 notebook lying open, its pages with abstract ruled lines only, a pen across it
objects.ID badge on lanyard: a work ID card in a clear plastic holder on a woven fabric lanyard about 20 mm wide; the card face is a slot, with no text, photo or logo
objects.plants: real houseplants drawn as their own species: a golden pothos trailing heart-shaped leaves, a snake plant's upright striped blades, a peace lily's glossy leaves and one white spathe, a rubber plant; in plain ceramic or terracotta pots with saucers
objects.window: the 1930s timber casement: a dark green-painted frame with cream-painted opening lights, side-hung lower lights and a row of small top-hung upper lights above a transom at about 1.7 m, the upper lights glazed with clear leaded panes in a square and diamond pattern of thin lead lines, the lower lights plain glass with slim glazing bars; a painted timber sill inside at 0.85 to 0.9 m; the glass shows the sky and the view, never a blank white
objects.radiator: a white steel double panel radiator about 0.6 m high, standing on two floor-fixed brackets about 0.1 m above the floor, with a valve with a round head at one end and a small bleed key socket at the top corner
objects.wall shelf: a single oak shelf about 0.8 m long and 0.2 m deep on two black steel L-brackets screwed to the wall
objects.cardigan: a knitted wool cardigan in slate blue hung over a chair back, its sleeves hanging down, soft folds at the shoulders
objects.dining table: a solid oak dining table 1.5 by 0.9 m, its top 0.75 m high and about 30 mm thick, on four square tapered legs joined by a plain apron; light wear and a few rings on the top
objects.dining chair: a wooden dining chair: four legs with a stretcher, a solid seat about 0.46 m high, a back of a curved top rail over three upright spindles; the chairs round one table are of two different designs
objects.kitchen: a fitted kitchen: cabinet doors painted sage green with slim brass bar handles, a 150 mm plinth, an oak worktop 0.9 m high and 0.6 m deep with a rounded front edge, a tiled splashback of small white rectangular tiles to about 1.35 m; a sink with a mixer tap under the window, a hob with a slim extractor hood over it, an oven door with a handle bar; a white electric kettle with a handle and spout on the worktop; a fire blanket in a red-tabbed wall pouch by the hob; a fridge in a tall housing with a plain door
objects.pendant light: a pendant: a ceiling rose, a fabric-covered flex and a spun-metal shade about 0.35 m across over a table, about 0.8 to 0.9 m above the table top
objects.sideboard: a low oak sideboard about 1.15 m long, 0.45 m deep and 0.8 m high: two doors and two drawers with round wooden knobs, on short tapered legs
objects.calendar: a wall calendar hung on a nail: a picture half above and a grid half below, both drawn as a slot (no numbers or words), a pen on a string
objects.laptop: a laptop about 0.32 by 0.22 m open on its own, the screen tilted back about 110 degrees, the back of the lid plain with no logo; a charging cable to the nearest socket
objects.school bag: a child's backpack about 0.4 m tall, with two shoulder straps, a front pocket with a zip and a grab loop, hung by its loop or lying on its side
objects.dog bed: an oval dog bed about 0.8 by 0.6 m with a padded raised rim and a cushion, slightly dented in the middle, a chewed rope toy in it
objects.garden doors: a pair of glazed timber doors to the garden, each leaf about 0.6 m wide and 2.0 m high in a dark green-painted frame, cream-painted leaves with slim glazing bars and a band of small leaded panes in the top rails, brass lever handles, a timber threshold
objects.sofa: a two-seat sofa about 1.8 m long and 0.9 m deep: a wooden frame on short tapered legs, two seat cushions about 0.43 m high, a back about 0.85 m high with two back cushions, rounded arms; upholstered in slate-blue wool
objects.coffee table: a low oak coffee table 1.1 by 0.55 m and 0.42 m high, a plain top on four short legs with a lower shelf for magazines
objects.rug: a flat-weave wool rug with a simple border, its corners slightly curled, lying flat on the floor
objects.floor lamp: a floor lamp about 1.6 m tall: a round weighted base, a slim brass stem, a drum shade of oat linen about 0.4 m across
objects.fireplace: the 1930s tiled fireplace: a surround about 1.2 m wide and 1.1 m high built of glazed tiles in stepped horizontal bands (buff and pale green), a narrow tiled mantel shelf, a small raised tiled hearth in front; the opening closed by a plain black panel holding a small electric fire
objects.router: a broadband router: a small white plastic box about 0.2 by 0.15 by 0.04 m standing upright, with a row of tiny status lights (dots only) and a cable at the back
objects.cushions and throw: square cushions about 0.45 m with soft rounded corners, piped edges and a dent where someone leaned; a knitted wool throw folded or draped with soft hanging folds
objects.print: a framed print: a plain thin oak frame with a pale mount, the picture an empty slot or a simple landscape with no figures, hung on two cords from the picture rail
objects.front door: the 1930s front door: a timber leaf about 1.98 by 0.84 m and 44 mm thick, painted deep sage green, with a small horizontal oval window of rippled glass high up under a little drip moulding and two long panels below it, a brass letter plate about 254 mm wide at about 0.8 to 1.0 m, a round brass knob and a lock; long narrow side panels of rippled glass either side in the same painted frame
objects.porch: a round-arched open porch: a semicircular brick arch of headers springing from plain brick piers, a recess about 1 m deep with plastered walls and ceiling, a red quarry-tiled floor one step up from the path with a bullnosed tiled edge, a small hanging lantern
objects.video doorbell: a video doorbell: a slim rounded rectangle about 130 by 45 mm and 25 mm deep, a round lens near the top and a round button with a thin ring of light below; mounted about 1.2 m above the step on the frame at the lock side of the door; no logo
objects.parcel: a corrugated cardboard box about 0.4 by 0.3 by 0.2 m, sealed with brown tape, a plain paper label (a slot, no writing), slightly dented at one corner
objects.wheelie bin: a wheeled household bin about 1.07 m tall and 0.58 m wide: a tapered dark grey body, a hinged flat lid with a front lip, a handle bar at the back over two wheels
objects.path and front garden: a front path about 1.2 m wide of red and buff quarry tiles in a chequer with a rope-edge border, lawn either side, a narrow bed with a hydrangea (big round heads of faded flowers) under the bay; a low brick front wall and a timber gate at the pavement

research: Real-space facts checked on 2026-10-15 (the 1930s semi: pre-war-housing.org.uk on the speculative semi's plan and UWE Bristol's Domestic Architecture 1700 to 1960 on casements with top-hung upper lights, porches, bays and tiled fireplaces; 1930s internal doors and picture rails: joinery retailers and homeowner reports; door, worktop, table, chair, sofa and coffee table sizes: UK door size charts and furniture planners; home DSE set-up: university and council home-working checklists; video doorbell height and letter plate size: installation guides and BS EN 13724 summaries; smoke alarms: LABC).
